. While reading out the contents of the FIR, learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the total disputed amount, as alleged by the complainant, is Rs.23 lakhs.

It is further submitted that an amount of Rs.5 lakhs has already been returned by petitioner No.1 - Kavita through hrough bank transaction, as also reflected in the compromise deed dated 20.03.2024 (Annexure P P-2).
Referring further to the allegations in the FIR, learned counsel points out that the complainant has also admitted of receiving an additional amount of Rs.6 lakhs in cash, which brings the total admitted amount to Rs.11 lakhs, apart from the car belonging to petitioner No.1, which is also in possession of the complainant.
It is further submitted that petitioner No.1 - Kavita is now all alone, having been deserted by her husband following the registration of the FIR, and is therefore unable to meet out thee liabilities independently.
Learned counsel states that the petitioners are ready and willing to join the investigation and fully cooperate with the investigating agency, and accordingly,
prays for the grant of anticipatory bail.
3.
Notice of motion.

4. On advance notice, Mr. Neeraj Madaan, Sr. DAG, Punjab, appears on behalf of respondent respondent-State and seeks time to file a reply.
5.
Adjourned to 26.09.2025.

sentences.text: 2 6. Taking into consideration that the matter arises out of a monetary dispute, that the petitioners are women, that the husband of petitioner No.1 is yet to be arrested, and that a part payment of Rs.11 lakhs has already been received by the complainant as per submissions of learned counsel for the petitioners, this Court deems it appropriate to grant interim protection to the petitioners.
Accordingly, the petitioner petitioners are directed to join the investigation as and when required to do so by the Investigating Agency.
In the event of their arrest, the petitionerss shall be released on interim bail, subject to their furnishing bail bonds to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer.

The petitioner petitioners shall also be abide by all the conditions laid down under Section 482(2) of BNSS, 2023 (earlier Section 438(2) Cr.P.C.).
7.
Besides, it is directed that petitioners would hand over their passport to the Investigating Agency or to Court concerned, if the possess..
Otherwise, would submit an affidavit, disclosing the fact that they do not possess any passport.

It is also directed that before leaving countr country any time during trial, petitioners would seek prior permission to the Court."
3.

Continuing his submissions, llearned counsel for the petitioners contends that in compliance of the order dated 09.07.2025, passed by this Court, petitioners petitioner have joined th the investigation, and have fully co-operated.
co operated.
Therefore, he prays for confirmation of the said interim anticipatory bail order.

4. Learned State counsel confirms the said averment made by counsel for the petitioners petitioner of joining the investigation on 18.09.2025 by the petitioners, petitioner , and submits that as of now,
custodial interrogation of the petitioners petitioner are not required for the purpose of investigation.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
6.

Since, petitioners have already joined the investigation and custodial interrogation is no more required; ad ad-interim bail order dated 09.07.2025, .07.2025, passed by this Court is hereby made absolute.
Accordingly, present petition is allowed.

However, petitioners shall continue to join the investigation as and when required required to do so and abide by all the terms and conditions laid down under Section 482(2) of BNSS, 2023.
7.
Accordingly, petition stands disposed of.
